source.author: Abraham Baer
source.title: Baal t’fillah oder Der practische Vorbeter
source.sourceLabel: R.H. and V. (Neujahrs- und Versöhnungstage in the accent chapter)
source.scope: Complete literal Genesis22:19 example from No113 second setting. A bounded High Holiday instrumental source study; no general accent-to-melody rule or Kinnor equivalence inferred.
source.labelEvidence: p37 margin R.H. and V.; p30 No107 spells out Neujahrs- und Versöhnungstagen. Preface pIX distinguishes 1.W./2.W. alternative settings from harmony.

notation.key: One flat (B-flat); printed B-natural in p37 and E-flat5 in p39 retained. No key normalization.
notation.ending: All texted notes and final eighth rest retained; no separate untexted coda is appended.
notation.performance: Written durations at the selected quarter-note tempo; source recitative timing is regularized. Modern equal temperament/instrument articulation are approximate.

underlay.status: Source-preserving draft, independent Hebrew/musical/phonological review pending.
underlay.method: Exact unchanged UXLC words and canonical IDs. Printed Latin lyric fragments remain per note. je/l' and ja/cha share their complete Hebrew syllables; fragments do not introduce extra Hebrew letters or phonemes.
underlay.crossWordNotation: p37 el / n'o is one unequal triplet and one slur across two words. IDs are verse-occurrence-scoped; repeated assignments remain independent.
underlay.pronunciation: The source Latin reflects the printed edition only; the two MAM text styles and their alternatives remain independent. No phonemes, singing voice, recording times or source-edition equivalence is assigned.

review: Manual native-scan transcription and independent bar arithmetic; qualified musical/Hebrew-underlay review pending. No phonological grammar inferred.
sourceRights: 1894 publication, public domain; faithful library image crops. No modern arrangement, recording or proprietary material imported.
